hints: Acceleration on a velocity-time graph is represented by the gradient of the velocity-time line segment.
The train accelerates from rest ($u = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$) to its cruising speed of $16\text{ m s}^{-1}$ in $40\text{ s}$.
walkthrough:
Find the acceleration during the first $40\text{ s}$ as the gradient of the velocity-time graph from $(0, 0)$ to $(40, 16)$:
$$a = \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t} = \frac{16 - 0}{40} = \frac{16}{40} = 0.4\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the kinematic definition of uniform acceleration as the rate of change of velocity:
$$a = \frac{v - u}{t}$$
From the velocity-time graph, the train starts from rest ($u = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$) and reaches maximum speed $v = 16\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at time $t = 40\text{ s}$.

Substitute the values directly into the acceleration formula:
$$a = \frac{16 - 0}{40} = \frac{16}{40}$$
Divide numerator and denominator by $8$:
$$a = \frac{2}{5} = 0.4\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

hints: The total area under a velocity-time graph represents the total distance travelled ($9040\text{ m}$).
The graph forms a trapezium with parallel sides of length $600\text{ s}$ (the total journey time shown on the time axis) and $T$ (the time at constant speed), with height $16\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Use the area formula $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2}(600 + T) \times 16 = 9040$ and solve for $T$.
walkthrough:
The total distance between stations corresponds to the area of the trapezium formed by the velocity-time graph:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2}(b_1 + b_2)h = 9040$$
where the bottom base is the total time $600\text{ s}$, the top base is the duration of constant speed $T$, and height is $16\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
teacher_walkthrough:
State the geometric property that the area under a velocity-time graph equals the total displacement:
$$\text{Distance} = \text{Area of trapezium} = \frac{a + b}{2} \times h$$
Here, the base on the time axis is $600\text{ s}$, the parallel top base (duration at constant speed $16\text{ m s}^{-1}$) is $T$, and the maximum velocity height is $h = 16\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Substitute the total distance $9040\text{ m}$ and height $16\text{ m s}^{-1}$ into the area formula:
$$\frac{600 + T}{2} \times 16 = 9040$$
$$8 \times (600 + T) = 9040$$

Divide both sides by $8$:
$$600 + T = \frac{9040}{8} = 1130$$
Subtract $600$ from both sides:
$$T = 1130 - 600 = 530\text{ s}$$

hints: Find the duration of the deceleration phase by subtracting the acceleration time ($40\text{ s}$) and constant speed time ($530\text{ s}$) from the total time ($600\text{ s}$).
The deceleration phase forms a right-angled triangle under the velocity-time graph with base equal to the deceleration time and height $16\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Calculate the area of this triangle: $\text{Distance} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$.
walkthrough:
Determine the duration of the deceleration phase:
$$t_{\text{decel}} = 600 - (40 + 530) = 600 - 570 = 30\text{ s}$$

Calculate the distance travelled during deceleration as the triangular area under the graph:
$$s_{\text{decel}} = \frac{1}{2} \times t_{\text{decel}} \times v_{\text{max}} = \frac{1}{2}(30)(16) = 15 \times 16 = 240\text{ m}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Calculate the time spent decelerating to rest in the final stage:
$$t_{\text{decel}} = t_{\text{total}} - t_{\text{accel}} - t_{\text{cruise}}$$
Substitute the known time intervals:
$$t_{\text{decel}} = 600 - 40 - 530 = 30\text{ s}$$

State the formula for distance travelled under constant deceleration to rest:
$$s = \frac{u + v}{2}t$$
During this stage, initial speed is $u = 16\text{ m s}^{-1}$, final speed is $v = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and duration is $t = 30\text{ s}$:
$$s = \frac{16 + 0}{2} \times 30 = 8 \times 30 = 240\text{ m}$$
